overview: This bill, the Rural Small Business Resilience Act, would require the Small Business Administration (SBA), the federal agency that helps small businesses, to make sure people in rural areas hit by a declared disaster have full access to its disaster assistance, such as low-interest disaster loans. Within one year, the SBA's Office of Disaster Recovery and Resilience would have to take steps such as targeted outreach and marketing materials aimed at rural residents and businesses. The bill also fixes a numbering error in the Small Business Act. As of July 29, 2025, the Senate Small Business Committee had approved it and it was placed on the Senate calendar.
for: Supporters say rural residents and businesses often don't learn about or can't easily reach SBA disaster help, and targeted outreach would help them recover faster after disasters.
against: Critics say the bill mostly directs outreach the SBA could already do on its own, without adding funding or changing loan terms that may matter more to rural borrowers.
